attempt: Term 'declarative sentence' might be a new definition no rule gives.
reason: Every element is stated: IV.6.4.2.2.1 p1 makes USE a compiler directing verb, IV.6.4.2.2.2 p1 makes a compiler directing sentence a single such statement ended by the period, VII.4.6.3 SR1 puts USE 'in a sentence by itself'. The glossary adds no condition; the term is never used in a rule.
quoted: consisting of a single USE statement

attempt: Minimum of one section, or that each declarative must begin with USE (SR1 says 'when present').
reason: IV.6.4.1.1 p1 gives the grouping, the opening DECLARATIVES and the closing END DECLARATIVES; the USE SR1 of each module gives header, USE, then zero or more paragraphs; the DECLARATIVES format brackets state the section set. No condition left over.
quoted: the first of which is preceded by the key word DECLARATIVES

attempt: Different scope from IV.6.4.2.4 p1.
reason: IV.6.4.2.4 p1 is the same sentence verbatim including the folio pointer.
quoted: Any statement which includes its explicit scope terminator

attempt: Descending order for SEARCH ALL / OCCURS KEY not stated.
reason: SORT GR2b and MERGE GR3b state highest to lowest by the comparison rules; OCCURS KEY GR4 says ascending or descending order is determined by the comparison rules. The glossary adds no further condition.
quoted: starting with the highest value of key

attempt: The period requirement is only in the formats, not in a named rule.
reason: The unit's one normative content, the header indicates the beginning of a division, is VI.2.3.3 GR1 / X.2.3.3 GR1 verbatim; the word combination and period are the fenced general formats the unit itself lists.
quoted: that indicates the beginning of a division

attempt: Dynamic access scope: records PLACED only nonsequentially but OBTAINED either way, within one OPEN.
reason: Unit says records are placed into the file in a nonsequential manner and obtained in a nonsequential manner and in a sequential manner during the scope of the same OPEN. VIII.2.4.4 GR4 says only 'may be accessed sequentially and/or randomly': it omits the placement asymmetry (no sequential placement) and the same-OPEN scope. Doubt goes to a reader.
quoted: in a nonsequential manner and obtained from a file in a sequential manner

attempt: Which symbols are editing characters.
reason: The unit fixes the set (B 0 + - CR DB Z * $ , . /) that the rules' term 'editing characters' draws on (VI.5.9.5 GR8 'including any editing characters', VI.5.15.4 GR1, XIII.3.19.4 GR1 'excluding any editing characters'). VI.5.9.4 GR6a lists PICTURE symbols allowed in numeric edited items including 9, P, V, which are not editing characters here, and GR8 explains symbol functions, not membership. No named rule states the membership.
quoted: fixed two-character combination belonging to the following set

attempt: The unit states that this symbol belongs to the set of editing characters (and its name).
reason: Each table line is one member of the set p83 introduces ('belonging to the following set'). The named rules give each symbol's function (VI.5.9.4 GR8, VI.5.9.5 GR4-8), not that it is an editing character; with p83 a row the lines are its data.
quoted: fixed two-character combination belonging to the following set

attempt: 77-level items are not 'subdivisions of a record', so IV.4.3.2 p2 would not cover them.
reason: IV.4.3.2 p2: 'those not further subdivided, are called elementary items'; IV.4.3.2.1 p5 says noncontiguous items are 'not themselves subdivided'. Same definition; no extra condition.
quoted: not being further logically subdivided

attempt: Period requirement only in format.
reason: Normative content is VI.2.4.4 GR1 / X.2.5.4 GR2 'indicates the end of the specified COBOL source program'; the period is the fenced format the unit introduces.
quoted: that indicates the end of a COBOL source program

attempt: Rules do not say which words are explicit terminators.
reason: IV.4.4.4 p1 (two types) and its table T1.1-T1.7 list the END-xxx words, each terminating its statement; nothing more in the unit.
quoted: terminates the scope of a particular Procedure Division statement

attempt: Item must be part of an external record; no 77-level external.
reason: X.1.3.4 p5 (subordinate item attains the external attribute) and p2 (may be referenced by any program that describes it) state both halves.
quoted: described as part of an external record

attempt: Constituent items referenced from any describing program.
reason: X.1.3.6 GR1 states the record may be referenced from any program that has described it; the constituent items follow by X.1.3.4 p5.
quoted: whose constituent data items may be referenced

attempt: 'Accessible to one or more programs' differs from 'any program that describes it'.
reason: X.1.3.7 GR1 'may be referenced from any program which describes that file connector' with X.1.3.4 p2 (external = run-unit storage) states the same accessibility.
quoted: accessible to one or more object programs

attempt: Second sentence of IV.4.5 p1 differs.
reason: IV.4.5 p1 begins with the identical sentence; the unit has no more.
quoted: defined and named by the implementor

attempt: Missing condition on which reserved words.
reason: IV.4.2.2.2.3 p1: 'Figurative constant values are generated by the compiler and referenced through the use of the reserved words given below'; the unit's 'certain reserved words' is that list, the folio pointer adds none.
quoted: A compiler generated value referenced

attempt: Digit position stated by PICTURE or USAGE rules, or SR rather than GR.
reason: No catalog rule defines the term or says it equals a character position under USAGE DISPLAY (grep of all rules). It defines meaning, so GR (IV.3.2).
quoted: amount of physical storage required to store a single digit

attempt: Entry defined by an FD or data description rule.
reason: No numbered rule defines the general term 'entry'; it defines meaning, so GR.
quoted: Any descriptive set of consecutive clauses

attempt: File defined by a rule.
reason: Only sort file (XI.1.2.1 p1) and merge file (XI.1.2.2 p1) are defined; 'file' itself is not. GR meaning.
quoted: A collection of logical records
